cells.tense: Right now you are building the frame around the thing you finished.
cells.ask: Write down the three rules this next thing runs on, then read them aloud to one person who has to work inside them.
cells.core:
You carry a thing all the way to what it actually made, then build the frame that holds it. What you finished sits in front of you and you are not sentimental about it. You can see what it needs next, and what it needs is usually a structure with edges, so other people can stand in it.

That part is working. The load got carried, and you are already turning what you learned into something that holds. You can say out loud what the structure is for, and when you say it, people can build against it instead of guessing. The frame still fits the room, and it fits because you measured.
cells.sheetLine: You finished it, and you are building what holds it.
cells.verb: carrying what you started all the way to what it made
cells.place: where you build the frame that holds a mess

cells.tense: You are already living inside a structure that is not finished yet.
cells.ask: Pick one rule you enforce on something no longer in front of you, and drop it for a day without replacing it.
cells.core:
You are designing the frame before the thing it holds exists. Rules for a group that has not met. A system for a problem you have not reached. You got good at building structures that worked, so now you build ahead, and building has become the thing you do in place of the work.

The structures you make are still tight. They just do not have much inside them. The moment you are supposed to be in keeps getting spent on the next container you want ready. A frame that is doing its real work does not require you hovering over it. Let a rule you already set stand on its own and find out what it does without you.

cells.tense: You used to say what this next thing was supposed to be, and you have not said it since.
cells.ask: Say out loud to one person, once, what this next thing is supposed to become, in plain words, without softening it.
cells.core:
You look at the raw thing you made and cannot see how to hold it. You are standing at the place where the new shape gets chosen and are not picking. What you made is still with you. You know it better than anyone does.

The part that stopped is the part where you say what it is for, out loud, before anyone agrees. That part does not need courage. It needs one other person listening while you hear your own voice put a shape under the thing. The shape is already there in your hands. It stays there while you wait.

cells.tense: You are holding people inside a shape you set without noticing you made it.
cells.ask: Name out loud, once, the one arrangement you set that others treat as given, and say you set it.
cells.core:
The rules the people around you follow, you set. The order things happen in, what counts as done, who speaks when. You don't experience yourself as having chosen any of that. It looks like how things are. You put the frame under it, and the day you did went by without getting marked.

Nothing is wrong with the structure. It is holding better than you think. What is missing is the part where you say you built it. Not a speech, just one arrangement you set that others treat as given, said out loud as yours. That is what makes a frame visible without making it a cage. The shape you made is already carrying weight in the room.
cells.sheetLine: You set the shape they are standing in. Say so.
